# @kitlangton/solid-motion

[Motion](https://motion.dev) for SolidJS. The same animation engine, springs and
gestures, with a `motion.*` API that uses Solid's fine-grained reactivity.

```bash
npm install @kitlangton/solid-motion solid-js
```

```tsx
import { motion } from "@kitlangton/solid-motion"

<motion.button
  animate={{ scale: active() ? 1.1 : 1 }}
  whileHover={{ y: -2 }}
  whileTap={{ scale: 0.95 }}
  transition={{ type: "spring", visualDuration: 0.22, bounce: 0.1 }}
/>
```

## Presence

Keep `AnimatePresence` mounted and pass a child factory, so the exiting element
can be retained until its exit animation finishes:

```tsx
<AnimatePresence when={open()}>
  {() => <motion.div initial={{ opacity: 0 }} animate={{ opacity: 1 }} exit={{ opacity: 0 }} />}
</AnimatePresence>

// Switch between keyed children
<AnimatePresence when={true} presenceKey={tab()}>
  {() => <motion.div exit={{ opacity: 0 }}>{tab()}</motion.div>}
</AnimatePresence>
```

## Gestures and drag

`whileHover`, `whileTap`, `whileFocus`, `whileDrag`, `drag`, `dragConstraints`
(box or `{ current: element }`), `dragElastic`, `dragMomentum` and
`onDragEnd(event, { offset, velocity })` follow Motion's semantics.

## Motion values

`useMotionValue`, `useTransform`, `useSpring`, `useVelocity`,
`useMotionValueEvent`, `animate`, and `useReducedMotion` (returns an accessor).
Motion values update the DOM directly without re-running components.

## Notes

- As in Motion for React, `visualDuration` takes effect only alongside `bounce`
  (use `bounce: 0` for no overshoot; negative values overdamp).
- Layout animations (`layout`, `layoutId`) are not implemented yet.
- Built on `motion-dom@14`. Gesture implementations are adapted from
  `framer-motion@14.0.0` (MIT).
